It is not longer because the inventory is finite, drilling is discretionary and not yet committed, and the single-basin, commodity-driven margin tends to revert within a cycle or two.

Oil-price volatility makes the range wide.

business_model.claim: PrimeEnergy is an independent oil and natural gas company. It makes money by acquiring, developing and producing oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids (NGLs) from properties located in the United States.
quotes: We are an independent oil and natural gas company engaged in acquiring, developing, and producing oil and natural gas.

business_model.claim: Its customers are unaffiliated purchasers, independent marketing companies and midstream companies. Essentially all revenue comes from sales to them, so purchaser credit and payment timing affect cash flow.
quotes: We derive essentially all of our revenues from the sale of our oil, natural gas and NGLs to unaffiliated third-party purchasers, independent marketing companies and midstream companies.

business_model.basis: stated in the F2 income statement member lines
business_model.claim: Oil is the largest revenue line. For the nine months to the latest quarter, oil sales were 106,884, natural gas was (4,946), NGLs were 19,320 and oil and gas service was 5,591. Total revenues were 126,850 (table in thousands of dollars).

A smaller services line sells well-servicing support to the company's own operated wells and to third parties. It brings in revenue (5,591) and carries its own field service expense (3,803) (table in thousands).
quotes: Through our subsidiaries Prime Operating Company and EOWS Midland Company, we act as operator and provide well-servicing support operations for many of the onshore oil and gas wells we operate, as well as for third parties.

business_model.basis: stated in P4 tables; the third-quarter comparison is inferred from F2
business_model.claim: Oil revenue moves with realized price and volume. In the nine months, the average oil price was $84.63 against $65.08 a year earlier, while barrels sold fell to 1,263,000 from 1,562,000. Oil revenue was 106,884 against 101,651 (table in thousands).
quotes: Current-year net income reflects lower oil and natural gas liquids production volumes, partially offset by higher realized prices for those products.

business_model.claim: Natural gas revenue depends on regional Permian pricing. Pipeline takeaway constraints pushed the nine-month average realized gas price to $(0.65) from $1.13, even though volumes rose. The third-quarter price recovered to $2.20.
quotes: The decline in realized prices was primarily attributable to pipeline takeaway constraints in the Permian Basin, where insufficient transportation capacity relative to regional production has resulted in negative or significantly reduced natural gas prices.

business_model.claim: The company uses oil derivatives to stabilize cash flow but does not apply hedge accounting, so changes in fair value hit earnings. The income statement shows a third-quarter loss on derivative instruments of (6,536) (table in thousands). This lowered net income although it is not an operating cost.
quotes: The Company does not enter into derivative contracts for speculative purposes and does not designate these contracts as accounting hedges.

business_model.claim: Depreciation, depletion and amortization (DD&A) is the largest cost line. For the nine months it was 46,609 against 55,242 a year earlier. Lease operating expense was 28,109 and production and ad valorem taxes were 9,904 against 7,498. Total costs and expenses were 97,483 (table in thousands).
quotes: Depreciation, depletion and amortization of the cost of proved oil and gas properties are calculated using the unit-of-production method.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P4 and F3; the link to cash balance is inferred from F3

quotes: substantially all of our exploration and development activities are conducted through joint drilling and operating agreements with others engaged in the oil and gas business.

The Company expects development expenditures during 2026 to be substantially lower, reflecting the timing of drilling and completion activities and its participation in projects operated by third parties.

While these contracts reduce the Company’s exposure to declining oil prices on the hedged volumes, they also limit the Company’s ability to benefit from increases in market prices above the contracted fixed prices.

risks.basis: figures stated in the filings; the link to future revenue is inferred
risks.claim: Oil volumes and capital spending are falling, so near-term production growth depends on wells not yet completed. Nine-month oil barrels sold fell 19.14%, and capital expenditures were 18,001 against 67,956 a year earlier (table in thousands). Management expects 2026 development spending to be substantially lower.
quotes: The Company expects development expenditures during 2026 to be substantially lower, reflecting the timing of drilling and completion activities and its participation in projects operated by third parties.

risks.basis: the cut is stated in the 8-K; the risk mechanism is stated in the 10-K, and its materiality is inferred
risks.claim: The bank cut the borrowing base from $115,000,000 to $105,000,000 in August 2026. The facility is the stated backstop for any cash flow deficiency, and the base can fall further if prices or reserves decline.
quotes: On August 3, 2026, PrimeEnergy Resources Corporation, (The Company), amended its borrowing base agreement with Citibank, N.A., decreasing the borrowing base from $115,000,000 to $105,000,000.

risks.basis: ownership is stated in the 10-K; the minority-holder and liquidity effects are inferred
risks.claim: Ownership is concentrated and the share count keeps shrinking through buybacks. The CEO beneficially owns about 55.4% of fully diluted shares, and 10,585 was spent on treasury stock in nine months (table in thousands). This could affect minority holders and trading liquidity.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, Mr. Drimal beneficially owns, including the effect of stock options and voting arrangements, approximately 55.4% of the Company’s fully diluted shares.
